title: How the Army treated Lester; "Break up Basie"; Jones as infantry soldier
summary: Jones says the Army treated Lester Young shamefully and suggests an effort to break up Basie's band; he himself chose infantry and refused to play drums.

bands.name: Glenn Miller Army Air Force Band

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Then why was Glenn gone? Overnight?
Glenn had the Air Force Band...
I know that. What I'm trying to find out is why there were no preparations for Lester to go any place.
That's a strange question, Milt.

You were supposed to go... there was a certain thing like that, Jo, that I remember quite well. I was with Cab Calloway when my turn came and there was also that same thing that I was supposed to go. The musicians black or white - Sy Oliver, most of us - were given first preference of the service -
You remember Artie Shaw had the other band that went to Honolulu. with Dave Tough.
So I wanted to know what happened to Lester, why nobody was there to see what branch of the service did he go into?
Soldier, infantry. That's the way they assigned him.
Was it of his own volition?
Of course not, what did he have to do. He had nothing to do with that. All I know is, with 5 1/2 million people in the Army at that particular time, there's no way

in the world that I would have treated a dog like the United States Army treated Lester Young and I can get it from Jefferson, Missouri; I can get it from the Adjutant General; I can get it from anywhere. What they did for Lester Young was unspeakable, because it became a personal thing. But you must remember this, Milt, you remember how they used to have a slogan, "Break up the Yankees"? Well, they had a slogan, "Break up Basie". So now if we can get Buck Clayton, if we can get Jack Washington - get the key figures out - if we can get Jo Jones, if we can get Lester Young out of Basie's band - then we can control Basie's band, for the simple reason Vaughn Monroe had given up his band and told everybody goodby, "I'm going down to take my physicial." When he went down there he was rejected, but he became a millionaire.
But Buck Clayton had a very fine position in the Army.
J: Yes, but..
H: What I'm concerned is why didn't Pres have one.
NO,
Oh, of course not.
And you didn't do too bad.

I didn't do anything, but what I did - it's a matter of record what I did and what I had to do. What I was in a position to do, because I didn't have to go into the Army; I had a choice. I said, "I'll take the infantry." I refused to play drums. I soldiered in the Army, Milt.
Oh you did? Then like Pres you also soldiered.
JONES 106
No, I soldiered, but the way they was treating Lester Young was unfair, because I didn't run into Lester any more until I was at Fort McClellan, Alabama.
Then neither one of you went into the musical branch of the service.
